title: MP4 text-to-protein design yields ATP-active proteins, including one with a novel fold
summary: The transformer MP4 maps plain-language prompts to protein sequences. The study reports two experimentally validated de novo designs that were expressible and thermostable and showed ATP binding and hydrolysis in vitro. X-ray structures at 1.30 Å and 1.77 Å showed that one design adopts a fold not previously observed in the authors’ structural comparisons.
organization: 310 AI; University of California, Berkeley; McGill University; Arctoris

evidence.tested: The study reports two experimentally validated de novo designs that were expressible and thermostable and showed ATP binding and hydrolysis in vitro.
evidence.unknown: Only two designed proteins are described as experimentally validated in the abstract; this is an early proof of concept, not a demonstrated general success rate. ATP binding and hydrolysis are in-vitro results, not a novel physiological function or therapeutic effect. The source describes one fold as novel; no claim is made that both structures are novel.
evidence.ai_role: MP4 converted natural-language protein specifications into candidate sequences. Researchers evaluated 96 prompts in silico, selected candidates, expressed and tested designs, and solved two crystal structures. The source attributes the designed sequences to MP4; experimental teams established expression, thermostability, ATP binding/hydrolysis and structural novelty.
